dataset.title: Truckee River Continuous (15 minute) Water Quality Monitoring: collected by the North Central Region Office, California Department of Water Resources, 1998-2025

associatedParty.organizationName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

abstract.para: The California Department of Water Resources (DWR) Water Quality Evaluation Section (WQES) provides technical expertise and program support for regulatory compliance, water operations, emergency response, and environmental restoration. The dataset details information at 15-minute intervals from 4 monitoring stations, using Xylem’s Yellow Spring's Instrument's (YSI) EXO2 and 6600 multiparameter sondes to document individual water quality measurements of multiple parameters. The dataset also details information at 15-minute intervals from 8 monitoring stations, using ONSET HOBO Water Temperature Pro V2 Data Loggers to document individual water quality measurements of water temperature.

The data set consists of water quality data collected to fulfill a DWR agreement to implement and manage a Water Quality Monitoring Plan (WQMP) for the Truckee River Watershed between 1998 and 2025. The stations included in this data package are: Truckee River at Bridge 8 (TRB8), Truckee River above TTSA (TRTT), Little Truckee River Above Boca (LAB), Truckee River at Farad (FAR), Truckee River Above Donner Creek (TrkAbvDnc), Donner Creek Above Truckee River (DncAbvTrk), Truckee River Below Donner Creek (TrkBlwDnc), Truckee River Above Prosser Creek (TrkAbvPr), Prosser Creek Above Truckee River (PrAbvTrk), Truckee River Below Prosser Creek (TrkBlwPr), Truckee River Above Little Truckee River (TrkAbvLtk), Little Truckee River Above Truckee River (LtkAbvTrk). Parameters measured at TRB8, TRTT, LAB and FAR include water temperature, dissolved oxygen, turbidity, pH and specific conductance at 25 C. Only water temperature was collected at the other stations. (Note: Sondes were removed from TRB8, TRTT, LAB and FAR on 10/09/2024 and replaced with ONSET HOBO data loggers that only measure water temperature)

The purpose of the project was to identify any water management impacts to Truckee River water quality from the implementation of the Truckee River Operating Agreement (TROA), prior to the tributary flowing into Nevada. It is important to note that the start dates and subsequent equipment upgrades vary between stations and equipment leading to discrepancies in the dataset’s date ranges.

description.para: Data collection for this project ended August 21, 2025. All data published has been QAQC'd
I. Continuous Water Quality Collection Methods

All water quality parameters were collected using Xylem YSI EXO2 multiparameter water quality sondes (https://www.ysi.com/exo2) or YSI 6600 Series multiparameter water quality sondes (https://www.ysi.com/file%20library/documents/manuals/069300-ysi-6-series-manual-revj.pdf) or ONSET HOBO Water Temperature Pro v2 Data Loggers (https://www.onsetcomp.com/sites/default/files/2025-05/10366-J%20U22-001%20Manual.pdf?_gl=1*1tbu4v3*_up*MQ..*_gs*MQ..&gclid=EAIaIQobChMI69D2m_z6lAMV3iGtBh1S4DpoEAAYASAAEgIn9vD_BwE). Water quality parameters included in this dataset are: water temperature (°C), specific conductance at 25 °C (SC [µS/cm]), pH, dissolved oxygen (DO [mg/L and %]), and turbidity (FNU). Data readings were collected at 15-minute intervals. The field stations included in this data set are TRB8, TRTT, LAB, FAR, TrkAbvDnc, DncAbvTrk, TrkBlwDnc, TrkAbvPr, PrAbvTrk, TrkBlwPr, TrkAbvLtk and LtkAbvTrk. The North-Central Regional Office (NCRO) is the data manager and performs a daily preliminary visual inspection of the data to verify data transmission to CDEC (for LAB and FAR) and that the data reported is within expected ranges for the conditions. NCRO additionally performs a monthly visual and computational inspection to identify irregular data or other non-representative outliers. Stations are serviced at a minimum of once per month for equipment maintenance and to perform quality control checks.

NCRO adheres to strict calibration standard operating procedures. Sondes are calibrated by NCRO in a laboratory setting within 72 hours of a field deployment. Sensor functionality for water temperature, and SC are verified prior to calibration in standards of known quality.

At the end of a field deployment, fouling error measurements are recorded for all parameters. The purpose of taking fouling error measurements is to calculate fouling error that the removed YSI EXO2 sonde accrued during deployment. This is fouling error data obtained by recording pre-clean and post-clean readings from the removed sonde alongside a freshly calibrated verification sonde in a stable environment, i.e., a 5-gallon bucket of ambient water (https://pubs.usgs.gov/tm/2006/tm1D3/pdf/TM1D3.pdf). Pre-clean readings represent the YSI EXO2 sonde’s performance in the environment and post-clean readings represent the YSI EXO2 sonde’s performance free of environmental interference from fouling and debris.

A post-measurement calibration drift check is completed in a laboratory setting for every sonde that returns from deployment using a known calibration standard. The post-measurement calibration drift check quantifies calibration sensor drift that occurred over the course of the deployment for each water quality parameter.

Field data are reviewed by field crews prior to leaving each field site. Data sheets are reviewed again by data entry staff when field data is manually entered into a Microsoft Access database, which also features customized error-flagging and data validation check tools.

Datasets are rated by a total error to account for calculated fouling error and calibration drift error (fouling error + calibration drift error = total error). Datasets also undergo visual quality checks within DWR’s KISTERS Hydstra continuous database management system used for collection of high frequency continuous time series data for water quality, surface water, groundwater and tidal station types. Each parameter is visually inspected for outliers and periods of noise. Data that is determined to be non-representative of the environment is either removed or flagged as not available. This dataset is filtered for data which have passed NCRO’s WQES data validation procedures. Data in this dataset that did not pass validation or was not collected due to equipment malfunction are reported as “NA”.
Data was downloaded from DWR’s Hydstra continuous database management system and processed and compiled in R version 4.5.3.

Field data are collected and recorded on paper datasheets by NCRO field crews, then entered into a Microsoft Access database. Paper datasheets are archived in binders that are stored at the West Sacramento DWR office, and electronic copies are archived on DWR/NCRO Network drives. Continuous raw datasets are downloaded to YSI Kor Software or ONSET HOBO Software and exported as a comma-separated values (CSV) file which are stored on DWR/NCRO Network drives. Final continuous datasets are archived within DWR’s KISTERS Hydstra continuous database management system and published publicly to DWR’s Water Data Library (https://wdl.water.ca.gov/).

project.title: Water Quality Monitoring at the Division of Regional Assistance, North Central Region Office, Water Quality Evaluation Section in the California Department of Water Resources

abstract.para: Truckee River Water Quality Monitoring Plan

This project was established to collect data to: 1) fulfill a DWR agreement to implement and manage a Water Quality Monitoring Plan (WQMP) for the Truckee River Watershed; 2) identify any water management impacts to Truckee River water quality from the implementation of the Truckee River Operating Agreement (TROA), prior to the tributary flowing into Nevada; 3) provide regional baseline water quality data for TROA implementation and for local agency support.

A multi-state and agency agreement, TROA is used to manage water operation releases from regional dams to improve water temperature control within the Truckee River. In 2008, the final TROA Environmental Impact Statement and Environmental Impact Report (EIS/EIR) were certified and no significant impacts to water quality in the Truckee River Watershed were found. While the EIS/EIR found no significant impacts DWR has been collecting continuous baseline water quality data in the Truckee River Watershed for 10 years in anticipation of TROA implementation and continued that monitoring through August 2025.
